knowledge_scope.secondary_website_features: The website may contain account, dashboard or Earn pages, but these support the ecosystem and must not replace the website's primary information-hub identity in editorial content.
knowledge_scope.dashboard_scope: Dashboard, website wallet-linking implementation and withdrawal implementation are outside the current editorial synchronization phase. Do not publish new technical claims about them until they are explicitly re-reviewed.
source_priority: For current Telegram Mini App behavior, use the latest executable apex-miner application/API/database logic.
For public project identity, tokenomics, contract address and roadmap communication, use the current reviewed apxn-landing public project pages and this knowledge file.
For general blockchain, BSC, Web3 and security education, use only approved official external source profiles configured by the blog pipeline.
Do not use older marketing text when it conflicts with current executable behavior or the current reviewed website.
Do not use the APXN Blog itself as the primary source of truth for new APXN project facts.

facts: The server validates Telegram Mini App initData using Telegram HMAC verification.
Telegram authentication data is accepted for up to 24 hours in the current implementation.
The implementation rejects excessively large initData and timestamps too far in the future.
User identity is derived from the verified Telegram user payload rather than trusting a client-supplied Telegram user ID.
article_evidence: APXN uses Telegram Mini App initData as the authentication input for protected application requests. The server does not simply trust a Telegram user ID sent by browser code. It parses the signed initData payload, verifies the Telegram HMAC signature with the bot token and then derives the trusted user identity from the verified Telegram user object.

The current shared authentication helper limits initData length to reduce abuse before cryptographic parsing. It also checks that the received Telegram hash has the expected SHA-256 hexadecimal form and uses timing-safe comparison for the calculated and received signature values.

The current APXN policy accepts Telegram authentication data for up to 24 hours and rejects authentication timestamps that are too far in the future. These checks are application-security controls and should be described as current implementation details rather than universal requirements for every Telegram Mini App.

notes: The current application tracks APXN Points as an in-app participation balance.
The automated blog must describe this as an in-app points system, not proof-of-work blockchain mining.
A successful claim updates the user's points balance and last-claim timestamp through server-side database logic.
The current optimized claim RPC keeps the 12-hour cooldown and performs an authoritative re-check under a row lock before granting a reward.
article_evidence: The current APXN community product uses a mining-style points experience inside Telegram. The balance tracked by the application is APXN Points. The word mining describes the user experience of accumulating points over time; the current claim action is not proof-of-work, does not solve cryptographic puzzles and should not be described as blockchain consensus mining.

The base APXN Points rate in the reviewed implementation is 0.00025 points per second. The user's effective rate can be higher when active referred friends qualify for the referral-speed bonus. The server-side claim logic uses the effective rate when calculating the amount credited after an eligible claim.

A normal APXN Points mining claim has a 12-hour cooldown, represented in the database logic as 43,200 seconds. Requests made before the cooldown expires do not receive a new reward. The API can return the remaining retry time so the interface can show when the next claim becomes available.

When a claim appears eligible, the database logic performs an authoritative re-check while protecting the user's mutable balance row. This is important because two requests can arrive close together. The protected second check prevents concurrent requests from both awarding the same elapsed mining period.

The reward formula is based on elapsed seconds multiplied by the total mining rate. The total mining rate begins with the user's base mining rate and can include active-referral bonuses. The resulting APXN Points are added to the existing balance and the successful claim time becomes the new last-claim timestamp.

The APXN Points balance is an application participation balance. It must not be described as a bank deposit, a guaranteed cash balance, a guaranteed investment return or a currently withdrawable cryptocurrency balance. Token distribution, conversion and withdrawal are separate future project stages that require their own official activation.

The 12-hour claim rule and the rate formula are current product mechanics, not permanent promises. If the application later changes its rate, cooldown or reward model, articles must be updated from current executable logic rather than preserving old numbers merely because they appeared in an earlier article.

Editorial content may use phrases such as APXN Points mining experience, collect APXN Points or mining-style claim system when writing for users. Technical explanations should immediately clarify that the system calculates and records points in the application backend rather than performing proof-of-work blockchain mining.

notes: A valid referrer must already exist and cannot be the same Telegram user.
The registration referral bonus is credited to the newly referred user when the referral is valid.
The inviter's ongoing benefit comes from active-friend mining-speed boosts rather than a duplicated registration bonus.
article_evidence: A new APXN Telegram Mini App account is registered through server-side logic after Telegram initData has been validated. The server derives the Telegram user identity from the verified payload and passes the trusted identity to the registration RPC rather than accepting an arbitrary browser-supplied account identifier.

The current welcome-bonus system uses the number of already registered users before the new account is created. Accounts joining while the existing total is below 10,000 receive 10,000 welcome points; the next tier below 50,000 receives 5,000; the next tier below 100,000 receives 2,500; later accounts receive 1,000.

The welcome tiers are APXN Points rewards inside the application. They should not be described as guaranteed token allocations, guaranteed monetary value or a guaranteed airdrop amount. The tiers describe the current registration reward logic and may change if the product rules are updated in the future.

Telegram referral data arrives through the Mini App start parameter. The registration API validates the referral value before it is used, accepts only a positive numeric Telegram identifier within the supported database range and rejects self-referrals. Invalid referral input does not become a trusted referrer relationship.

When the referral is valid under the registration logic, the newly referred account can receive a 1,000-point referral bonus at registration. This registration bonus belongs to the new user. It is separate from the inviter's continuing benefit from active-friend mining-speed bonuses.

The inviter does not receive an unlimited duplicated welcome reward simply because another account registers. The ongoing referral mechanic is tied to whether referred friends remain active according to the mining-claim activity window. Articles should keep the registration bonus and active-friend rate bonus as two different mechanisms.

Country information can be recorded when a newly created account is registered, but that country value is informational. It must not be used in articles as proof of nationality, citizenship, identity verification, KYC status or eligibility for a future token distribution.

Whenever an article discusses early-user rewards, it should distinguish verified registration bonus tiers from separate marketing campaigns, Early Access badges or future airdrop eligibility rules. A campaign percentage or first-N-user promise must not be inferred from the welcome-bonus tiers unless that rule is stored separately as a current official policy.

The registration tier boundaries depend on the number of users already present when the new account is created, so an individual user's welcome reward is determined by the tier active at registration time. Articles should explain the thresholds directly and avoid promising that a later user can retroactively receive an earlier tier.

daily_checkin.cycle_behavior: After day 7, the reward cycle returns to 100 points while the streak can continue.
daily_checkin.missed_day_behavior: If the previous check-in was not yesterday, the next successful check-in starts a new streak at day 1.
daily_checkin.duplicate_prevention: Atomic database row locking plus server-side duplicate protection.
article_evidence: The APXN Daily Check-In is a server-backed points reward that operates on UTC calendar dates. A user can receive one successful check-in reward for a given UTC day. A second attempt on the same UTC date is rejected as already claimed instead of adding another reward.

The check-in reward follows a repeating seven-day reward pattern. Day 1 awards 100 APXN Points, day 2 awards 200, then 300, 400, 500, 600 and 700 on day 7. If the streak continues to day 8, the reward amount cycles back to 100 while the streak counter can continue increasing.

A streak continues only when the previous successful check-in was on the previous UTC date. If the user skips a day or the stored previous date is otherwise not yesterday, the next successful check-in begins a new streak at day 1 and uses the corresponding 100-point reward.

The check-in logic locks the user's database row while evaluating and writing a successful reward. This protects the balance and streak from concurrent requests that might otherwise attempt to claim the same daily reward at nearly the same time.

The Daily Check-In reward is APXN Points and should be described as an engagement reward inside the current ecosystem. It is not an on-chain staking yield, blockchain block reward, guaranteed investment return or direct proof of future token allocation.

Because the system uses UTC for the authoritative date, a user's local midnight does not necessarily define a new APXN check-in day. User-facing articles can explain that availability follows the system's UTC-day logic instead of promising a reset at midnight in every local timezone.

The seven-day cycle is a reward schedule, not a seven-day expiration of the entire APXN account. Missing a day affects the streak progression and next reward tier; it does not by itself imply deletion of the user's previously accumulated APXN Points.

Articles should distinguish the Daily Check-In from mining-style claims and social tasks. Mining claims use an elapsed-time and mining-rate calculation, while Daily Check-In uses a calendar-day streak reward. They can both increase APXN Points but they are different product mechanics with different eligibility rules.

The check-in streak and reward are written through trusted server-side database logic rather than allowing the browser to choose its own reward amount. This distinction matters for security explanations: the interface requests the action, while the backend decides whether the day is eligible, calculates the reward and updates the balance.

daily_tasks.claim_frequency: Once per UTC day per task
daily_tasks.important_note: The backend records the daily task reward but does not independently prove every external like or repost action. Editorial content must not overstate external-action verification.
article_evidence: APXN daily tasks are separate from the Daily Check-In and from one-time social tasks. The current daily task reward logic recognizes Telegram and Twitter/X task identifiers and awards 100 APXN Points for a successful eligible task claim.

A daily task can be rewarded once per UTC day for its task type. The server-side reward logic records the daily completion state so repeated claims for the same task and date do not continuously add points.

The application interface can direct a user toward an external Telegram or X activity before the claim action becomes available. The existence of an interface delay or a completion button is not the same as independent cryptographic or API proof that every external like, repost or view occurred.

Editorial content must avoid saying that all external social actions are technically verified. The safe description is that the APXN backend enforces the reward claim rules and completion state, while verification of a particular external action depends on the specific task implementation.

Daily task rewards are application points, not payment for investment activity. The current 100-point value belongs to the product's engagement rules and can be changed by later application updates. Blog articles should identify it as current behavior and should not convert the number into token value or fiat value.

tasks.server_verification: Telegram getChatMember is used before the reward path.
Telegram getChatMember is used before the reward path.
No external X follow verification is established by the reviewed reward RPC.

article_evidence: One-time social tasks use a different reward path from the recurring daily tasks. In the reviewed APXN logic, channel, group and Twitter/X social task types each use a 500-point reward when the task is successfully claimed for the first time.

Telegram channel and Telegram group membership can be checked by the server with Telegram membership information before the reward path. This gives the project a server-side way to confirm supported Telegram membership states rather than relying only on a button click in the browser.

The X follow task should be described more carefully. The reviewed APXN reward database can record the Twitter/X task as completed, but this does not establish independent X-platform follow verification. Articles must not claim a level of external verification that the current code does not demonstrate.

Once a one-time social task is stored as completed, the reward RPC does not award the same one-time task again. The completion flags and points balance are updated together through trusted server-side database logic rather than allowing the browser to directly increase its own balance.

The one-time social-task system is designed to prevent the same supported task from being rewarded repeatedly after its completion flag has been stored. This differs from daily tasks, which can become eligible again on a new UTC day. A comparison article should explain both the reward frequency and the different verification boundaries.

referrals.active_friend_definition: A referred account whose last successful mining claim was within the previous 24 hours.
referrals.speed_bonus_per_active_friend: 5% of the inviter's base mining rate
referrals.country_role: Informational only; it does not affect authentication, rewards, mining or referral eligibility.
article_evidence: Every APXN user can share a Telegram Mini App referral link that includes the inviter's Telegram user identifier in the startapp parameter. When a new user opens the Mini App through that link, the registration path can evaluate the start parameter and create a referral relationship if the value is valid.

An APXN referred friend becomes active for mining-speed purposes when that referred account has a successful mining claim within the previous 24 hours. The active-friend definition is based on recent claim activity, not merely on whether the friend once registered or opened Telegram.

Each active referred friend adds five percent of the inviter's base mining rate to the inviter's effective mining rate. The formula uses the base rate as the reference for every friend, so the total rate is base rate plus active-friend count multiplied by five percent of the base rate.

The referral-speed bonus changes the rate used when the inviter later makes an eligible APXN Points claim. It is not a direct transfer from the friend's balance and it should not be described as taking points away from the referred user.

A referred account that has not claimed within the most recent 24-hour window no longer counts as active for the current speed calculation. If the friend later makes a qualifying mining claim again, the active-friend count can reflect that recent activity in later calculations.

The referral relationship and active status are application mechanics for APXN Points. They must not be described as guaranteed token yield, staking APY, passive investment return or proof of future token allocation. The benefit is an in-app points accumulation-rate increase under the current rules.

The friend list can include the referred user's first name, stored country code and last-claim information. The country field is informational only and does not change the referral reward formula, authentication status, mining eligibility or future token eligibility.

The APXN referral system includes two separate ideas that articles must not combine: a valid referral can give a new user a registration referral bonus, while the inviter benefits over time through active-friend mining-speed boosts. These mechanisms have different recipients and different conditions.

Referral articles should explain that the current five-percent rule is calculated from the inviter's base mining rate for each active friend. They should not invent tier multipliers, maximum friend limits or extra cash rewards unless current executable logic or an official policy explicitly introduces them.

The referral link format and activity rules are current product behavior and can change with future product updates. New articles should be generated from the latest verified code rather than copying historical referral numbers from older promotional posts.

roadmap.source_policy: The detailed Telegram Mini App roadmap and the simplified website roadmap describe the same project direction at different levels of detail. Use the detailed phases below for chronology and the public summary for general website wording.
article_evidence: The APXN roadmap is a forward-looking development plan, not a guarantee that every milestone will happen on an exact date. Articles should describe future phases with terms such as planned, targeted or scheduled and should avoid language that turns roadmap timing into a contractual promise.

Current feature status must be determined independently from roadmap dates. Some community features can exist before a roadmap phase that mentions their formal launch or expansion. Conversely, a future roadmap item does not become live merely because the calendar reaches the quarter printed beside it.

The 2026 foundation centers on the Telegram community experience, APXN Points, check-ins, tasks, referrals and the official project website. The website should present this as the current ecosystem foundation while keeping token distribution, withdrawals, Presale / ICO, Testnet, staking and Mainnet clearly separated as later stages.

The 2027 roadmap focuses on engagement growth, application improvements, rig or upgrade concepts, security infrastructure and a phased Presale / ICO target beginning in Q2 2027. Until an official activation notice exists, the Presale / ICO must continue to be described as planned rather than live.

The 2028 roadmap moves toward platform optimization, token preparation, later listing and points-transition announcements and the planned Apex Testnet stage. Naming DEX or CEX support in a roadmap does not itself confirm a listing relationship with any specific exchange.

The roadmap places the Apex Testnet launch target in Q4 2028 after earlier token-preparation and listing-announcement stages. Testnet articles can explain what the project plans to test, but they must not claim that a public testnet network, explorer or developer endpoint exists before a verified launch.

The 2029 roadmap includes Testnet expansion, staking preparation and implementation targets, Mainnet preparation and a planned Mainnet launch. Staking rewards, validators, nodes, native Mainnet APXN and a Mainnet Explorer must remain future-tense until those systems are actually deployed and verified.

Roadmap summaries on the website can group detailed quarterly milestones into yearly sections as long as they preserve the same chronology and status. A simplified summary must not move a planned feature earlier, imply that a planned item is already active or introduce an exchange, price or partnership not present in verified sources.

If development priorities change, the roadmap can change. Blog articles about roadmap history should identify the version or review date they are based on and should not reuse obsolete dates after the official project roadmap has been updated.

The safest APXN roadmap article combines two layers: verified current product facts for what users can use today, and clearly labeled roadmap information for what the project intends to build later. This prevents readers from confusing an existing APXN Points feature with a future token, network or financial function.

The roadmap should also be separated from tokenomics. A token allocation percentage describes how the project currently plans to allocate supply, while a roadmap period describes when development or launch stages are targeted. Neither one, by itself, proves that a sale, listing, distribution, withdrawal or network launch is currently available.

automation_editorial_rules: Treat the Telegram Mini App and the website as two connected but different surfaces: the Mini App is the community APXN Points product; the website is the official project, token, blockchain, technical-information and news hub.
Use implemented facts as the highest-priority source for current Telegram Mini App behavior.
Use the exact term APXN Points when describing the current participation balance unless the article is explicitly discussing the APXN token.
Never merge APXN Points with the APXN token as though they are already the same withdrawable balance.
Never promise profits, guaranteed returns, guaranteed token price, guaranteed listing date, guaranteed exchange listing, guaranteed point-conversion value or guaranteed eligibility.
Never state that pressing Claim performs blockchain consensus mining. Explain that the Mini App calculates and records ecosystem points programmatically.

Never present a roadmap item, Soon feature, disabled upgrade, staking feature, Testnet, Mainnet, Presale / ICO, token distribution or withdrawal as already live unless the knowledge status is updated after verification.
Do not publish a live APXN Presale / ICO price or purchase instruction while presale_ico_status is Planned / Not Live.
Do not describe BscScan visibility as an independent smart-contract audit.
Do not claim wallet persistence or withdrawal-address binding for the Telegram Mini App until that implementation is specifically verified.
Dashboard and website wallet/withdrawal implementation are outside the current editorial synchronization phase; do not infer or publish new implementation claims about them.

When discussing Telegram tasks, state that channel/group membership can be server-checked; do not claim that X follows, likes or reposts are technically verified when the current code does not establish that.
Country information is informational and must not be presented as proof of identity, citizenship, KYC or eligibility.
For tokenomics, describe the percentages as the current official project allocation plan rather than a guaranteed financial outcome.
For roadmap content, clearly separate current implemented features from future project targets.
APXN News must come from a current approved official APXN update source and must not be invented from model memory.
Every article must contain useful educational or informational value beyond promotion.
Include an appropriate non-financial-advice disclaimer on tokenomics, presale, market, listing or digital-asset risk topics.
Block automatic publication whenever an article requires a fact marked verify_before_publish or blocked_auto_publish.
Do not use old blog articles as evidence for a new APXN fact when current code or current official project information says something different.
